title: Spelling List 6
ruleLine: the lazy uh at the heart of a word. Ten of these fourteen have the letter marked for you; the sheet leaves the last four to find.
chartBtn: every way this list spells the schwa

tips.listen: Listen for the lazy uh in the middle — that is the schwa, and it is the rule this week.
tips.boxes: Remember the rule — one letter in this word is only saying uh.
tips.reveal: The schwa letter is in pink. That is the part the test is looking for.
tips.plain: The sheet leaves this one unmarked on purpose. The schwa is in there — finding it is the job.

chart.head: The schwa spelled y
chart.note: this year's letter. A y doing the work a vowel usually does.

chart.head: The schwa spelled a, e, i, o, u
chart.note: one word for each of the five vowels, in order. Every one of them says uh.

chart.head: The schwa hiding in an ending
chart.note: -al and -le. Two endings you have met before, both of them uh.

chart.head: Find it yourself
chart.note: port = to carry, and two the teacher chose. These four are not marked on the sheet — say each one slowly and listen for the uh.

words.sent: After one summer of lessons she was ___ enough to play without looking at her hands.

words.def: the combining of separate parts to form a whole
words.sent: The report was a ___ of everything four different teams had found.

words.def: a person who is hopeful and confident about how things will turn out
words.sent: Only an ___ would pack shorts for a week in that weather.

words.def: musical notes sounded together to make a pleasing effect
words.sent: The two voices moved in ___ and the whole room went quiet.

words.def: a middle point between two extremes
words.sent: Between shouting and whispering there is usually a sensible ___.

words.def: a strong, repeated pattern of movement or sound
words.sent: You could hear the ___ of the drums three streets away.

words.def: a careful examination of the parts of something, or of how it is put together
words.sent: His ___ of the game showed exactly where it had been lost.

words.def: a tube with a plunger and a needle, used to push fluid in or draw it out
words.sent: The nurse filled the ___ and told him to look at the ceiling.

words.def: having to do with the government or the public affairs of a country
words.sent: The town meeting turned ___ the moment somebody mentioned the budget.
Every ___ in the museum case had a small number beside it.

words.def: the act of forcing a foreigner to leave a country
words.sent: The lawyer spent a year fighting the ___ of a family who had lived there for decades.

words.def: a close and easy relationship in which people understand each other and talk well together
words.sent: The new coach built a ___ with the team faster than anyone expected.

words.def: the use of an object or an image to stand for something larger than itself
words.sent: The ___ of the storm in that chapter is hard to miss.

words.def: the main figure in a story or a real situation; the champion of a cause
words.sent: The ___ of a story is not always the one you like best.
